# A window's `visible` is a two-way prop, and `open` and `close` assign it.
# `details` binds it to `shown`, so closing the window writes `shown`; `other`
# binds nothing, so the window keeps it in a cell of its own, which a read off
# its `#id` names. Both hosts print the same.
#
# testdata/window_visible.txtar is the code.

[!headless] skip 'needs the headless compositor go tool verify provides'

[gtk4] sngl build --lang go --platform gtk4 -o gtk4 app.sngl
[gtk4] exec ./gtk4/app
[gtk4] cmp stdout want.txt

sngl build --lang go --platform fyne -o fyne app.sngl
exec ./fyne/app
cmp stdout want.txt

-- want.txt --
shown=true other=true
shown=false other=false
shown=true other=true
-- app.sngl --
import go "sngl:language/go"
import time "sngl:time"
import ui "sngl:ui"

#[go.native("os", "os.Exit")]
func exit(code int)

#[go.native("fmt", "fmt.Println")]
func println(s string)

var (
    shown = true
    ticks = 0
)

time.timer(interval=200ms, @tick {
    ticks += 1
    println("shown={shown} other={other.visible}")
    if ticks == 1 {
        details.close()
        other.close()
    }
    if ticks == 2 {
        details.open()
        other.open()
    }
    if ticks == 3 {
        exit(0)
    }
})

ui.window #details(title="Details", :visible=shown) {
    ui.text(value="{ticks}")
}

ui.window #other(title="Other") {
    ui.text(value="other")
}
